gap: No result ChatGPT got states that every three-added-screen Aura extender under $600 (eight models, $449 to $579 on Aura's store on 2026-11-21) needs a driver install on first use, that the two Aura cards ChatGPT showed at $499 and $519 read $489 and $499 that day, or that UPERFECT's own three-screen 16-inch at $599.99 is a pre-order shipping at the end of November.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages (the UPERFECT blog and mobilepixels.us/products/trio, which returned HTTP 429 to me three times and was not read) plus theofficejournal.com, the PCWorld KYY review and our own dealectric.com/best-triple-laptop-screen-extender. The UPERFECT blog lists eight models with undated prices, four of them $699.99 to $799.99, and names a driver only for the BE14BF. The Office Journal gives no dollar prices and no video path beyond 'plug and play'. Our own page already has dated prices and video paths for the Trio 3 Pro, BE14BF, Xebec, FOPO S788 and Cevaton Z2, so the two-added-screen half is not new. None of them prices the $449 to $599.99 three-added-screen band, mentions Aura at all, or flags the UPERFECT pre-order. The other eight result pages were not opened.
decides: Two added screens: confirms the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro ($407.99, driver-free on two video-capable USB-C ports) over the UPERFECT BE14BF, which is $18 less and lighter but needs a driver for its single-cable connection. Three added screens: the $600 limit admits the FOPO S788 only through our link ($540 with code FOPO; $599.99 store price), and the Aura Triple Go Max 16" at $489 undercuts it by $51 with the same count and size, both driver-based. So the S788 cannot be called the price winner; it holds the segment only as the three-screen model we can link, with FOPO's stated macOS M1/M2/M3 support. Over the line and left out: Xebec Tri-Screen 3 ($699), Aura's $609 to $629 models, INVZI MagHub Quad 14 and Quad Max, Monduo 16 Pro Duo, FOPO S999 ($1,099.99).
